name: Chris H. Senanayake
title: Dr.
tagline: Process chemist, drug developer and champion of green, sustainable manufacturing.
role: Founder and Chief Executive Officer, TCG GreenChem, Inc.
summary: Dr. Chris H. Senanayake is a process chemist whose career spans more than three decades at Merck, Sepracor, Boehringer Ingelheim and, today, TCG GreenChem, the company he founded. He has been instrumental in bringing several medicines to market, including Crixivan, Lunesta, Jardiance, formoterol and desvenlafaxine, and is recognised internationally for developing practical, sustainable manufacturing routes to active pharmaceutical ingredients.
bio: Chris H. Senanayake was born in Sri Lanka, where he earned a Bachelor of Science degree with First Class honours. After moving to the United States he completed an M.S. in synthetic chemistry at Bowling Green State University under Professor Thomas Kinstle, and in 1987 received his Ph.D. from Wayne State University under Professor James H. Rigby. His doctoral work centred on the total synthesis of complex natural products, including the ophiobolanes, and delivered the first total synthesis of grosshemin in the guaianolide family.

His industrial career began at Dow Chemical before he joined Merck's Process Research group, where he contributed to the development of Crixivan, one of the first HIV protease inhibitors. At Sepracor he led process development for medicines including Lunesta, formoterol and desvenlafaxine.

In 2002 he joined Boehringer Ingelheim Pharmaceuticals in Ridgefield, Connecticut, and for fifteen years served as Vice President of Chemical Development, leading a large team of scientists and engineers responsible for routes to clinical and commercial APIs, including Jardiance.

In 2018 he became Chief Executive Officer of AstaTech (Chengdu) BioPharmaceutical Corporation and founded AstaGreen Chem, Inc. in Richmond, Virginia. In October 2019 he was appointed Chief Scientific Officer of TCG Lifesciences and founded TCG GreenChem, Inc., a US-based CDMO focused on green and sustainable chemical process development, where he serves as CEO.

He is the co-author of more than 500 papers, patents, book chapters and review articles, and an inventor on more than 115 patents spanning synthetic organic chemistry, asymmetric catalysis, process development and the design of improved chemical entities.

medicines.name: Crixivan
medicines.contribution: Developed the practical asymmetric synthesis of cis-1-amino-2-indanol, the chiral building block that made one of the first HIV protease inhibitors manufacturable at scale.

medicines.name: Lunesta
medicines.contribution: Led process development for the single-enantiomer sleep medicine, delivering a scalable route to the active (S)-isomer.

medicines.name: Brovana
medicines.contribution: Process chemistry for the single-isomer (R,R)-formoterol bronchodilator.

medicines.name: Pristiq
medicines.contribution: Contributed to the process development of the active metabolite of venlafaxine as a medicine in its own right.

medicines.name: Jardiance
medicines.contribution: As VP of Chemical Development, led the chemistry organisation that delivered the commercial manufacturing route for the SGLT2 inhibitor.

awards.title: Siegfried Gold Medal
awards.detail: For the development of practical processes for active pharmaceutical ingredients and contributions to process chemistry.

editorial: Editorial Advisory Board, Organic Process Research & Development (ACS)

research.title: Practical asymmetric synthesis
research.text: Chiral amines, alcohols and sulfoxides are the backbone of modern medicines. His group developed general, low-cost methods for making them in enantiopure form, including the modular tert-butanesulfinamide and related sulfinyl auxiliaries and the cis-1-amino-2-indanol platform behind Crixivan.

research.title: Catalysis and ligand design
research.short: Ligands that make hard reactions practical.
research.text: The P-chiral BIBOP and dihydrobenzooxaphosphole ligand families enabled asymmetric hydrogenations, Suzuki–Miyaura couplings and C–H functionalisations robust enough for manufacturing, along with nickel, copper and rhodium catalysed methods for building quaternary and atropisomeric stereocentres.

research.title: Process development for APIs
research.text: Route selection, optimisation, impurity control and scale-up for active pharmaceutical ingredients across HIV, CNS, respiratory and metabolic disease, taking candidates from first-in-human supplies through commercial launch.

research.title: Green and sustainable chemistry
research.short: Fewer steps, less waste, lower cost.
research.text: TCG GreenChem was founded on the principle that the most sustainable process is also the most economical one. Catalysis over stoichiometric reagents, telescoped steps over isolations, and benign solvents over chlorinated ones, applied to real manufacturing problems.

facts.label: Field
facts.value: Process chemistry · Asymmetric synthesis · Green chemistry

philosophy: The best process is the one a plant can run safely, every day, at the lowest cost to the patient and the planet.
